p1n1: We know why patients delay or miss cancer care. Research shared with us in this challenge shows it: fear, costs, health literacy.
p1n3: Most cancer patients in Finland are around seventy, and one in three people over seventy-five is not online.
p1n4: Meet CareCatalyst, for Finland's wellbeing services counties. They already hold the appointment data. Now they see who is stuck, and can ask why: for example, with a simple phone call to Eero.
p1n5: Counties pay once. Updates, once. No subscription. Research partners, companies like AstraZeneca, could fund the rest, and receive only anonymised, aggregated patterns, so research can adapt.
p1n6: But we go one step further. The center of gravity is shifting. Just as everyone has a phone today, soon everyone will have a personal agent.
p2e1: …and the usual dog food for Jenny, please.
p2a1: Eero, your back has hurt for three weeks, and you saw the orthopaedist last week. I can't diagnose, but a doctor should check this. Shall I book a check-up?
p2e3: Getting there is hard for me. I can't walk far. And honestly… I'm a bit scared.
p2a2: Don't worry. Finland already has help for this. Some care can come to you, and for the clinic, Kela covers most of the taxi. How about tomorrow at eight, before bingo with your friends?
p2n1: The center of gravity is moving: towards a future where everyone gets equal care, with the help of technology.
